question: Your team commits a project-scoped .mcp.json that defines the backend MCP server for the customer support agent, with its authentication token written as ${SUPPORT_API_TOKEN}. On most developer machines, the agent resolves billing disputes normally. On one new teammate's machine, get_customer, lookup_order, process_refund and escalate_to_human all appear, but every call to them fails with an authentication error. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: Environment variable expansion works only in user-level ~/.claude.json, so the ${SUPPORT_API_TOKEN} reference in .mcp.json is passed to the server literally.
options.reason: The guide describes environment variable expansion in .mcp.json as the way to manage credentials, and the agent works on the other machines with the same file.

options.text: Servers in a project-scoped .mcp.json apply only to the developer who committed the file, so the new teammate's agent lacks the server's credentials.
options.reason: Project-scoped .mcp.json is meant for shared team tooling, and the tools appear on the new teammate's machine, so the server configuration does reach that machine.

options.text: The four tools are discovered only when the agent first calls them, so those calls run before the server has finished authenticating.
options.reason: Tools from all configured MCP servers are discovered at connection time, and this timing idea would also fail to explain why the error appears on one machine only.

options.text: The SUPPORT_API_TOKEN environment variable is not set on the new teammate's machine, so the expansion in .mcp.json supplies no valid token.
options.reason: Environment variable expansion in .mcp.json takes each developer's credential from their own environment, so a missing variable on one machine leaves only that machine without a valid token.
